about: Each house front's picture read as bays and storey bands (px in its 1024-px picture, y down): bays [x0, x1] pier middle to pier middle, one window column each, 'door' where the ground floor has the front's door; bands: the rows a wall is built from (ground at the street, mid repeated for a taller house, top with the cornice); windows: the glass of every window [x0, y0, x1, y1], for the rooms seen through them (interiors.js). Read by eye from the pictures, 9 Nov 2026. 'hood': what the picture paints over the door, to be built out from the wall (js/world/facaderelief.js): kind 'gable' (x0, x1 its eaves' ends, cx, y0 its top, ye the eaves, y1 its underside) or 'flat' (the box x0, y0, x1, y1), depth in m, brackets [x0, x1, to y], cols [x0, x1, y0, y1, m proud], wall [x0, y0, x1, y1] plain wall to cover the painted one; A row's fourth number and the door's 'doorArch': the opening's head is an arch - its rise as a share of half the opening's width (1: a half circle), from its crown at the opening's top; the door [x0, y0, x1, y1] is the opening in the wall, its frame and transom with it (the six Moscow doors measured again on 12 Nov 2026: they had stood 8 to 20 px left of their doors). 'trim': a window casing's px at the sides, over the head and under the sill. shutters: [[x0, y0, x1, y1, side], ...] the shutters standing open beside its windows, side -1 left, 1 right (measure_shutters.py). A front measured to its openings (13 Nov 2026, msk2-white): its 'cols' and 'rows' (a row a window) are each window's hole in the wall's plane, to the outer edge of its reveal, and 'frames' {column: [x0, y0, x1, y1]} its painted frame inside the hole, the picture's reveal or soffit between the two; 'frameColours' {column: [r, g, b]} a frame that is not white (a glazed door's wood); 'doorCols' the columns whose opening is a door (a balcony's), modelled with the doors. The frames are models of their own (fixtures\frames_spec.py, frames_blender.py) and the window maps are made from the holes and frames (make_window_maps.py). 'eaves': the row a one-storey wall's top band ends at (under the cornice, over the windows' heads), joined there to the ground band's top. 'course': the string course's rows [y0, y1] in the ground band's top, modelled as a band proud of the wall. 'pilasters' (spb-ochre): {at: their middles' x px, half: half their breadth px, rows: [y0, y1] from the capital to the base, src: the one pilaster in the picture every one is cut from, depth m} - modelled standing out of the wall at each bay's joint (13 Nov 2026, the fronts straightened and made seamless). 'fittings' (msk2-white): what hangs on the wall or stands out of it, each [x0, y0, x1, y1] as the picture shows it (the balcony's slab, rail and brackets, 'balcony-edge' the rows of its slab's front edge, the French railings, lamps and plaques); 'models': the boxes the fittings' models are built to (fixtures\\fittings_blender.py, fronts/<front>-fittings.glb), each set where its bay and storey band stand (facaderelief.js); painted out of the picture, which keeps them in fronts/<front>-fixtures.jpg for the models' faces. 'doorParts': a door built as a model - each part [x0, y0, x1, y1, z from, z to (m out from the door's back), kind] ('wall': its face the front's picture there; 'brass'), and 'fan' [x0, y0, x1, y1, arch] a fanlight under an arch, flat at the back; set at the back of the door's opening (facaderelief.js). 13 Nov 2026: every front measured to its holes - 'cols' and 'rows' a window each, the hole in the wall's plane (out to where the picture's reveal ends: the surround is square to the wall, so the hole is centred in it), 'frames' the painted frame inside it (as the windows had been measured). 'frameModels': the front's windows' frames are models of their own (fronts/<front>.glb). A hole is widened past its painted frame only where the picture's reveal there is in shade against the surround's face beyond it (a frame flush in its surround - Petersburg's ochre front - has none). 'models' a box or a list of boxes: a model standing at several places (a pediment over every window, the bars of every basement window), built to the first; 'pedSpec' a window pediment's apex, eaves, level cornice, rake and depth, an entablature's frieze, cornice and consoles; 'grilles' {name: v bars upright, h rails at shares of the height, lattice diamonds, z m out}; 'depths' {name: m} a plaque's or letter box's own; 'trimRows' [y0, y1] the rows the 'trim' is for; 'cut' the casing's boards cut to the carving's shape (fronts/<front>-cut.png).
